text_block_1: Classes are fundamental building blocks in object-oriented programming for structuring applications.  They serve as blueprints, defining the state and behavior of objects created from them.  Instantiation creates new objects, each exhibiting properties and actions defined by the class.  Object state is stored in fields, representing unique data for each instance.  Object behavior is encapsulated within methods, which define the actions instances can perform.
text_block_2: Class Declaration - uses the class keyword followed by the class name, encompassing members within its curly braces.
text_block_3: Fields (Attributes) - are variables defined inside a class, storing the unique state or characteristics of its objects.
text_block_4: Methods (Behaviors) - are functions declared within a class, encapsulating the actions and operations objects can perform.
text_block_5: Access Modifiers - control the visibility of classes, fields, and methods, supporting encapsulation principles.
text_block_6: Constructors - are unique methods responsible for creating new class instances and setting their initial state.
